messages:
Emma (support): Customer (Acme) escalated: Safari 16/17 intermittently shows partial EventSource output then stops. They see a bunch of data events, then a final empty event and the browser never reconnects. Happening from our hosted streaming endpoint behind a CDN prefetch layer. HAR attached.
Raj (oncall): Can you paste the root request/response headers from the HAR? thread_ts 1762123456
Emma (support): From HAR (redacted):
GET /v1/streams/abc123 HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer <token>
Accept: text/event-stream

Response:
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/event-stream
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
Cache-Control: public, max-age=60
Surrogate-Key: sfx-manifest

Note: CDN turns initial prefetch into 200 then subsequent client GETs get 304. Customer says Safari's EventSource sometimes uses prefetch/manifest which appears to truncate streams.
Anna QA: I see related nginx logs showing "upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream" around the same time window. dev proxy may be closing idle conns when edge returns 304.
Oliver (runtime): This sounds like two problems colliding: (1) CDN prefetch/manifest caching turning streaming endpoints into cacheable assets (bad) and (2) Safari's EventSource + prefetch behavior which can reuse or swallow connections. Fix is to make streaming routes uncacheable and send keepalives. Suggested headers:
- Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate
- Pragma: no-cache
- Vary: Authorization
- Surrogate-Control: no-store
Also ensure Transfer-Encoding: chunked and avoid Content-Length on streaming responses.
Small keepalive: send a comment line every 10s, e.g. `: keepalive

` to keep proxies from idling out.
Raj (oncall): @Oliver can we also add X-Accel-Buffering: no for customers behind CloudFront/CF-Workers/Netlify? Some reverse proxies buffer chunked responses and then emit 304s from cache. If the CDN prefetch does a HEAD/GET that populates cache with 200 then later GETs get 304, the browser may treat the stream as completed. We should explicitly mark these endpoints as uncacheable in our edge rules.
Oliver (runtime): Agreed. Add policy: any /v1/streams/* routes set no-cache headers at edge and do not add Surrogate-Key. Also change our edge CDN behavior to respect sse=false route tag that disables prefetching/prefetch registration.
Emma (support): Customer asks for a short-term workaround they can deploy client-side. Any suggestions?
Anna QA: Workaround: avoid EventSource in Safari for this endpoint. Use fetch() + ReadableStream to do controlled reconnects and ignore 304s. Example:
```js
// fetch streaming fallback
const res = await fetch('/v1/streams/abc123', { headers: { Accept: 'text/event-stream' } });
const reader = res.body.getReader();
const decoder = new TextDecoder();
let buf = '';
while(true){
  const { done, value } = await reader.read();
  if (done) break;
  buf += decoder.decode(value, { stream: true });
  // parse lines/events from buf...
}
```
This gives the app control to reopen on truncated streams.
Raj (oncall): For server fixes: set response header `Connection: keep-alive` and ensure our runtime sends a 1-byte keepalive periodically. Also confirm nginx/proxy timeouts (proxy_read_timeout) are longer than 30s for streaming routes. Put a small canary to test.
deploy-bot: canary/streaming-sanity failed: streaming endpoint returned 304 in canary environment - rollback flagged
Oliver (runtime): Noted. I'll push an edge config change to set Cache-Control override and add sse-no-cache tag. Also will add a small runtime guard to send `:keepalive

` every 12s and set Vary: Authorization. I will coordinate a canary deploy and tag affected customers.
Emma (support): I'll send customer the workaround + explain we plan an edge config change and runtime keepalive. Asking for permission to schedule a maintenance window if needed. :thumbsup:
Raj (oncall): Assigning follow-ups: @Oliver - runtime/edge fix (PR + canary)
@Anna - produce minimal repro steps + small HAR scrubbed for engineering
@Emma - customer comms and temporary client-side snippet.
Anyone else, react with :eyes: if you want to be looped in.
